findings.evidence: fields collect `street_address` and `postal_code` but there is no city or state/region field anywhere in the form
findings.fix: Add required "City" (autocomplete="address-level2") and "State/Region" (autocomplete="address-level1") fields between street address and postal code.
findings.violation: An address with no city or state/province field is incomplete and cannot be validated or used for shipping.

findings.fix: Omit autocomplete on the secondary phone field (or use a `section-*` prefix) so it isn't conflated with the primary phone's autofill value.
findings.violation: Using the same autocomplete token for the primary and secondary phone fields causes browsers to autofill the identical saved number into both fields, defeating the purpose of a "secondary" phone.

findings.fix: Remove the digit-only pattern or broaden it (e.g. `[0-9+\-\s()]+`) to accommodate common phone formatting.
findings.violation: This pattern rejects legitimate phone number characters like a leading "+", spaces, dashes, and parentheses, so many valid numbers will fail validation.

findings.evidence: `name="website" required="" type="text"` with no autocomplete attribute
findings.fix: Change to `type="url" autocomplete="url"` and make it optional, or remove the field if it isn't actually needed for a consumer account.
findings.violation: The field is typed as plain text instead of `type="url"` (losing URL keyboard/validation), lacks `autocomplete="url"`, and is required even though a personal outfitter account shouldn't need a company website.

findings.fix: Remove this field from new-account signup (or make it optional for existing members), and if kept, enforce it with `pattern="[0-9]{8}" maxlength="8"` plus visible helper text instead of relying on the placeholder.
findings.location: `<div id="row-member">`, `<input id="member-input" ... placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">`
findings.violation: A brand-new account signup is requiring a pre-existing 8-digit membership number, which a new user wouldn't have yet; additionally the "8 digits" rule is only stated in a placeholder (which disappears on input) and isn't enforced by `pattern`/`maxlength`.

findings.fix: Remove this required field from the signup flow, or clarify/relocate it to a context where the user would already have an account number.
findings.violation: Like membership number, this requires an "account number" that a user creating a new account cannot yet possess, and the label gives no indication what this number actually refers to.

findings.fix: Increase `size` to at least 8 - 10, or remove the `size` attribute and rely on CSS width.
findings.violation: A visible width of 3 characters is too small for most real postal codes (e.g. US ZIP+4 "12345-6789" or UK postcodes), causing the entered value to be clipped from view.

findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate options (keep a single "Overnight/Next-day" choice).
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" describe the same delivery speed, so the options are redundant and will confuse users choosing between them.

findings.evidence: `<label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label>` duplicates `<label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label>` earlier in the form
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate field, or if a distinct legal name is genuinely needed, rename the label to clarify the difference and give it a distinct autocomplete value.
findings.violation: Two separate required fields ("Full name" and "Your name") both map to `autocomplete="name"`, so browsers will autofill the same value into both, and users won't understand why a name is asked twice.

findings.fix: Remove the inline `font-size` override and let it inherit the form's default text size.
findings.violation: This required field's text is rendered smaller than the rest of the form's inputs with no stated reason, hurting readability/accessibility and visual consistency.

findings.evidence: `style="display:inline-block;float:left;width:140px"` and the plain-text input has no placeholder, pattern, or format hint
findings.fix: Remove the inline float styling (use the same layout approach as other rows) and add a placeholder or a `<select>` of time windows instead of free text.
findings.violation: The label uses ad hoc inline float/width styling inconsistent with every other row in the form, and the "Preferred contact time" input gives users no indication of the expected format (e.g. time of day vs. a time range).

findings.evidence: button sits inside the form between the organization/contact-time fields and the date-of-birth fieldset, with no visible associated behavior
findings.fix: Either remove the button or clarify its purpose with surrounding text/markup, and style it consistently with the rest of the form's controls.
findings.violation: The button's purpose and target are unclear, it has no apparent handler, and its bespoke inline styling is inconsistent with the unstyled `submit-btn`, making it a confusing, orphaned control in the middle of the signup flow.

findings.evidence: year options run only from `<option>1950</option>` to `<option>2009</option>`
findings.fix: Generate the year list dynamically (e.g. current year minus a reasonable minimum age) up through the current year, rather than a fixed 1950 - 2009 range.
findings.violation: The hardcoded year range excludes anyone born before 1950 (over ~76 years old) or after 2009 (under ~17), arbitrarily blocking both older and legitimately eligible younger users from completing signup.

findings.fix: Add `method="post"` (and an appropriate `action`) to the form element.
findings.violation: Without `method="post"`, the form defaults to a GET submission, which would place the password and other sensitive fields into the URL, browser history, and server logs.
